structured_output.hypothesis: If the claim holds, measured 3D surfaces of isotonic biconcave red cells will show mean curvature that varies strongly across the membrane (not constant), and the cells will become near-spherical in hypotonic medium.
structured_output.pass_criterion: On matched isotonic RBC 3D surface reconstructions, the coefficient of variation of mean curvature H over the surface (excluding the rim) is >= 0.5 for at least 90% of cells. In the hypotonic condition, the median sphericity index (36*pi*V^2/A^3) is >= 0.9 and exceeds the isotonic median by at least 0.1.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if the isotonic mean-curvature CV is < 0.2 for a majority of cells, which would mean the surface is close to constant-mean-curvature. It is also refuted if the median hypotonic sphericity is < 0.8 or does not exceed the isotonic median.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'surface of equilibrium' under surface tension alone corresponds to a constant-mean-curvature surface (a Delaunay surface). 'Diluted blood' corresponds to a hypotonic medium. 'Some other force' (osmotic inequilibrium, cholesterin-like fluid crystals) corresponds, in modern terms, to the spectrin-actin cytoskeleton and bending elasticity, but the test only checks the geometric prediction, not the mechanism. This is a modern reinterpretation of the geometry. The mechanism part of the claim (which force maintains the shape) cannot be decided by shape data alone.
structured_output.no_dataset_reason: I could not verify any public dataset of 3D red blood cell surface reconstructions (holotomography, confocal or scanning-probe) with matched isotonic and hypotonic conditions. Searches of Zenodo, figshare and Dryad found none. The closest source with isotonic and hypotonic RBC tomography is the PLoS ONE paper 10.1371/journal.pone.0262106. Its data availability statement says the datasets are not publicly available because of participant consent, and the only downloads are figure files. The arXiv papers 2409.20013 and 1404.2968 have no deposited data that I found. I will not name a dataset or identifier I could not verify.
